nora kim: Hi folks — married last week (yay!) and trying to add my spouse to medical + dental. Questions: 1) spouse lives in Seoul, can we add midyear? 2) carrier asks for proof of residency vs passport — what docs are acceptable? 3) I want to switch my Dependent Care FSA to cover childcare now that household changed — is that allowed as a QLE? Also curious how payroll handles retro premiums if I pick an effective date back to the marriage date. Thanks!

jackie (People Ops): Congrats @nora! Short answers: 1) Yes, marriage is a QLE — you have 30 days from the ceremony to enroll without exception. 2) For an international spouse we accept passport + marriage certificate. If the carrier specifically requests "proof of residency" provide a government-issued ID (national ID) or a utility/lease doc in spouse's name; if those are not available, let us know and we'll work with the carrier. Translated docs: certified English translation OR apostille is fine. 3) Dependent Care FSA: household status changes (marriage) are qualifying events that allow you to change elections midyear; you'll need to update the election in the portal and provide the QLE date.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: QLE window = 30 days. SSN is required by some carriers; you can enroll pending SSN but must supply it within 60 days if requested. Upload docs: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/dependent-add :information_source:

ryan (Payroll): Regarding prorate/retro: premiums prorate from the coverage effective date you choose. If you select an effective date that predates the last paycheck, payroll will process a retro deduction on the next pay run to capture missed premiums; we'll show a line item "retro premium adjustment". If you'd prefer the retro amount split over two pay periods, say so and we can request that.

jackie (People Ops): A couple of practical tips: name the files like kim_nora_marriage_cert.pdf and kim_spouse_passport.pdf so carriers match quickly. If the spouse's employer abroad has coverage, that doesn't block you from adding them here as long as the QLE reason is marriage; carriers may coordinate benefits if both plans pay for the same claim. For Dependent Care FSA tax treatment and limits, payroll/tax will confirm — @ryan, can we DM Nora a quick projection of max yearly vs what she'd need to switch? :slightly_smiling_face:

ryan (Payroll): Yup, I'll DM a projection. One note on FSA changes: switching midyear changes per-paycheck pretax withholding immediately (prorated) based on the new total election and remaining pay periods. If you already maxed out pretax contributions under the old election, we'll flag any potential overcontribution.

nora kim: Thanks everyone — uploading marriage cert + passport now. I'll DM @ryan for the projection. Appreciate the help! :heart:
